pipeline_name: Beni Suef-El Minya Oil Products Pipeline

validity.recommendation: No change needed; swap the two dead almalnews.com refs (Start/Length/Cost) for the live vetogate.com source that states the same figures.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/ROUTE/STATUS: confirmed by two independent sources. (1) Vetogate news article (2026-08-27 verified live, 2015-04-28 dateline), 'Construction of a pipeline to supply Upper Egypt with petroleum materials': EGPC ('the General Petroleum Authority') is finishing the 'Beni Suef-El Minya' pipeline within weeks; cost exceeds 450 million EGP; length 140 km; purpose is delivering petroleum derivatives/liquid fuel to Upper Egypt governorates including fuel for power stations. This is the SAME single citation (vetogate.com/1604707, cite_id cite_note-:0-1) that backs 8 of the gem.wiki page's assertions -- so on its own it is a single-source finding, not independent corroboration by itself. (2) Ministry of Petroleum official document 'مشروعات خطوط الخام والمنتجات البترولية' (petroleum.gov.eg, verified live, fetched and read in full) lists 'خط مازوت بني سويف / المنيا' (the 'Beni Suef/El Minya mazut line') by name among lines fully implemented/operating in the period 2014-2015 through January 2023 -- an independent, authoritative government source naming this exact route as completed/operating. Combined, existence + route (Beni Suef->El Minya) + operating status reach HIGH tier via two independent sources. CLASSIFICATION: the ministry document specifically labels this a MAZUT (heavy fuel oil) line, not a generic petroleum-products line -- consistent with GEM's 'Oil products (only)' Fuel value (mazut is a refined product, not crude), so no reclassification needed, but note the more precise commodity is mazut/heavy fuel oil for power-station and Upper-Egypt-governorate liquid-fuel supply, per both sources. PipelineType=transmission is reasonable for a 140 km inter-governorate products trunk; no evidence it is a gathering/feeder line. DUPLICATE: checked against the full 46-row Egypt-oil roster. No other row shares the Beni Suef<->El Minya route -- P7343 (Helwan-Beni Suef, 36 km) and P7342/P7316 (El Minya-Asyut) are adjacent segments of the same broader Upper-Egypt products corridor but describe different endpoint pairs, not the same physical pipe. No duplicate flag. ATTRIBUTION: Owner1=Egyptian General Petroleum Corp 100% is a reasonable default (EGPC runs the ministry's national products-pipeline programme this line belongs to) but neither source names EGPC specifically as this line's owner/operator -- it could equally be held by a EGPC subsidiary such as Petroleum Pipelines Company (PPC), which is the more usual operator of Egypt's inter-governorate products trunks. Flagging as a low-confidence attribution caveat, not proposing a change absent a source that actually names the operator. SPEC: Length=140 km and Cost=450,000,000 EGP are BOTH explicitly stated in the vetogate article, matching the sheet exactly -- but the sheet's existing [ref] for both cells is a dead almalnews.com URL (HTTP 404, confirmed). Proposing to swap that dead ref for the live vetogate URL, which states the identical figures. Diameter and Capacity are blank on the sheet; neither source gives a diameter or capacity figure, so left blank rather than forced. StartYear1=2015 is consistent with the vetogate article (published 2015-04-28, describing the project as about to finish 'within weeks') and falls within the ministry document's 2014/2015-Jan/2023 completed-lines window, but neither source states an explicit completion/start year -- treated as confirmed at MEDIUM tier (a single contemporaneous news source plus a consistent-but-non-specific government date range, not two sources each independently naming 2015).
